answer: Price admission on a convex bonding curve: each new identity must burn tokens to mint a seat, and the price climbs steeply with how many seats one funding source already holds. A lone honest joiner pays the cheap first sip at the oasis; an operator spawning a dune of clones from one treasury faces a crystal-clear, quadratically rising bill per extra head. The ledger traces funding roots, so splitting capital cannot dodge the curve, and flooding turns cost-prohibitive while genuine newcomers enter cheaply.
